sequence.description: Token exchange trust-anchor substitution: attempt to exchange a subject_token from the wrong issuer/connector and ensure Dex rejects it
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex token exchange must verify the submitted subject_token against the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS). A token minted under a different issuer must not be accepted when presented to this connector_id.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow rejection/acceptance to proof verification behavior.
Dex accepted a subject_token with an issuer not bound to the configured connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS substitution).
Dex produced a userinfo identity for an untrusted-issuer subject_token, indicating consumed proof semantics were not the verified proof.

sequence.description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt unsigned request object (alg=none) to override semantic auth parameters (redirect_uri/scope) and compare to a normal auth request. Secure behavior is explicit rejection or ignoring the unsigned request object.

sequence.description: Attempt to escalate scopes/claims via RFC8693 token exchange: obtain a limited-scope token, then exchange it while requesting expanded scopes (groups/profile/federated:id).
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged token must not contain claims/permissions beyond the upstream intent (originally granted scopes) and broker policy; expanded scopes in token_exchange should be rejected or not reflected in resulting claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control flow failed; cannot attribute token-exchange behavior to authorization binding vs misconfiguration.
Token exchange accepted expanded scopes and returned groups claim despite original scope lacking groups; indicates scope/authorization escalation beyond upstream intent.
